picks.why: At 11.6x trailing with EPS up 10.1%, Progressive is the cheapest sound business on the list: a disciplined underwriter whose float earns more as reinvestment yields rise, which partly hedges the Council's biggest risk of the 10-year pushing toward 5%.

At 17.2x trailing with EPS up 6.2% and 1.88% weekly volatility, PepsiCo is a Dividend King staple priced below its own usual multiple, and it suits the Council's defensive stance going into Jackson Hole and PCE.

At 17.7x, Regeneron is the only cheap way into healthcare, the Council's consensus opportunity, against roughly 25-40x for JNJ, TMO, VRTX and LLY, and it has a cash-rich balance sheet and the Dupixent franchise behind it.

A fortress money-center bank at 16.1x with EPS up 13.4% and the lowest volatility among the financials (1.8%), on the safe side of the synthesis's split between money centres guiding for stable credit and regionals under strain.

At 16.9x trailing with EPS up 6.9%, Disney is an investment-grade parks, content and sports business that is cheap next to its own history and sits outside both the AI-duration selling and the utility breakdown.

summary: Five cheap, sound businesses kept clear of the synthesis's danger zones: no utilities, nothing in the AI/semis complex with NVDA reporting Wednesday, the healthcare call taken through its cheapest name (REGN), and two rate beneficiaries (PGR, JPM) as a partial hedge if a hawkish Jackson Hole or a hot PCE sends the 10-year toward 5%. I passed on names that look cheap but whose trailing EPS may be inflated by investment gains, a breakup or the cycle (GOOGL, AMZN, HON, SM, VLO, CALM), and I took valuations from the table because the synthesis's price levels don't match it (LLY $950, JNJ $168 and NVDA $115 against closes of 1255, 270 and 215). I have no memory of how this week went and used none.
